question: A Project that a department has relied on for a year has never had its uploaded knowledge reviewed. Which two maintenance actions are appropriate? Select two.
options: A) Schedule a regular review so outdated documents are found before they cause wrong answers.
B) Update or remove documents that no longer reflect current facts before they mislead Claude.
C) Leave every old document in place, since more background material always improves the answers.
D) Replace the Project with a fresh one as soon as any single answer turns out to be wrong.
E) Ask Claude at the start of each chat to work out which uploaded documents are outdated.
correct_answers: A) Schedule a regular review so outdated documents are found before they cause wrong answers.
B) Update or remove documents that no longer reflect current facts before they mislead Claude.
explanations: Correct. Stale knowledge is a documented failure mode: Claude Academy's Projects guidance says outdated documents can lead to outdated responses, so a scheduled review is what catches that before it produces wrong answers.

Correct. Claude Academy's Projects guidance says to review and update project knowledge periodically because outdated documents can lead to outdated responses - updating or removing the stale ones is what turns a review into an actual fix rather than just a diagnosis.

Incorrect. Claude Academy's Projects guidance is explicit that outdated documents can lead to outdated responses, so accumulating background material without pruning it works against accuracy, not for it.
Incorrect. Rebuilding the whole workspace after one bad answer discards good context instead of curating the source at fault.
Incorrect. Claude cannot tell which uploaded document has been superseded; that judgment depends on knowledge it does not hold.
